name: Dequalinium

overview.mechanism: Antimicrobial activity has been studied in different local formulations; evidence from vaginal tablets and combination throat lozenges addresses different clinical questions [[DEQ-BV,DEQ-THROAT]].
uses: The local registry includes throat/oral-antiseptic products. The vaginal-tablet bacterial-vaginosis trial below is formulation-specific research and does not establish an oral-product indication [[DEQ-BV,DEQ-THROAT]].

evidence.title: Clinical evidence and limitations
evidence.intro: Study regimens are descriptions of research, not prescribing recommendations.

rows.design: Triple-blind double-dummy randomized noninferiority trial; 147 premenopausal adult women; one-month follow-up.
rows.intervention: Vaginal dequalinium tablets versus oral metronidazole for bacterial vaginosis.
rows.findings: Early clinical cure was 92.8% versus 93.2%; the prespecified 15-percentage-point noninferiority criterion was met.
rows.limitations: Short follow-up, broad margin, manufacturer involvement. This is vaginal-formulation evidence; it cannot establish efficacy of antiseptic lozenges or long-term recurrence prevention.

rows.design: Noninterventional observational study; 90 adults; before/after one exposure.
rows.intervention: Dequalinium plus cinchocaine lozenges versus different-agent spray or gargle.
rows.findings: Only 10% of lozenge-group samples showed reduced postexposure bacterial-growth intensity; the gargle performed better on this microbiological measure.
rows.limitations: Combination product, unblinded, no randomized allocation or placebo; 20-minute bacterial-density surrogate does not establish sore-throat symptom benefit or efficacy of dequalinium alone.

sources.citation: Efficacy of Dequalinium Chloride vs Metronidazole for the Treatment of Bacterial Vaginosis: A Randomized Clinical Trial. PubMed PMID: 38696172.

draft_notes: Source-linked descriptive findings and safety information only. Current local product information, contraindications, formulation-specific dosing and renal schedules require verification.

common: In the vaginal-tablet trial, reported treatment-related events included candidiasis, pruritus and headache. These findings are not an adverse-reaction inventory for throat lozenges [[DEQ-BV]].

renal: Neither local-formulation study defines a renal adjustment or dialysis regimen. Route-specific safety and contraindications require the actual product information [[DEQ-BV,DEQ-THROAT]].
